metadata.title: What key contextual factors contribute to students’ reading literacy among top-performing countries and economies? Statistical and machine learning analyses

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 student microdata for reading literacy and constructs an analytic sample restricted to three high-performing economies (B-S-J-Z/China, Singapore, and Macau) and, separately, compares against the full set of 79 PISA countries/economies. The manuscript does not report whether PISA sampling/survey weights or replicate weights were applied in the Shapley value decomposition and Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT) modeling. Because the paper does not specify weight variables (e.g., TOTWGT or W_FSTUWT) and because tree-based ML is often run without native complex-survey weight support, the weighting approach is unclear; analysts should verify in the supplementary materials or replication code whether weights were used. For PISA analyses, the recommended practice is to apply the provided sampling weights and account for the complex design when estimating uncertainty; however, this paper reports predictive fit (R2/RMSE) without detailing variance estimation under the survey design.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The study uses PISA 2018 reading literacy microdata and defines two analysis scopes: (1) a restricted student-level sample from the three top-performing economies (B-S-J-Z/China, Singapore, and Macau) and (2) a comparison using the full PISA 2018 dataset across all 79 participating countries/economies. For the restricted analyses, the analytic sample includes students from these three economies only. Students with reading literacy scores below 262 are excluded because PISA did not specify reading literacy levels for scores below that threshold. Missing values in the selected contextual factors are imputed using the median of each factor.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Reading (top-performing economies: B-S-J-Z/China, Singapore, Macau)
main_findings.performance_metrics: GBDT (B-S-J-Z, Singapore, Macau as a whole): R2 = 0.49, RMSE = 68.34. Shapley value decomposition relative contributions: metacognitive strategies 53.83% (assessing credibility 42.46%, summarizing information 21.33%, understanding and remembering 19.51%), ESCS 18.87%, reading motivation/attitude 27.30%.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Reading data for B-S-J-Z/China, Singapore, and Macau, the study leveraged Assessing credibility, Summarizing information, ESCS, Reading interest, and Understanding and remembering to predict reading literacy (PV1READ), finding that metacognitive strategies—especially Assessing credibility—were the most influential factors and that the final GBDT model achieved R2 = 0.49 (RMSE = 68.34). This indicates that strengthening students’ metacognitive reading practices (credibility evaluation and information summarization) alongside addressing socioeconomic disparities may be a high-leverage policy and instructional priority in high-performing education systems, though the study is cross-sectional and uses PV1READ as a single plausible value.

main_findings.performance_metrics: GBDT (all 79 countries/economies): R2 = 0.48, RMSE = 73.26. Top five factors by relative influence: Assessing credibility; ESCS; Summarizing information; Self-concept: perceived difficulty; Reading interest.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Reading data across all 79 participating countries/economies, the study leveraged Assessing credibility, ESCS, Summarizing information, Self-concept: perceived difficulty, and Reading interest to predict reading literacy (PV1READ), finding that Assessing credibility remained the strongest factor while Self-concept: perceived difficulty emerged as a key differentiator at the global level and the GBDT model achieved R2 = 0.48 (RMSE = 73.26). This indicates that curricula and teacher guidance should prioritize credibility evaluation and information summarization as broadly relevant reading competencies, while also tailoring support for students’ perceived reading difficulty to reduce achievement variation internationally, though causality cannot be inferred from the cross-sectional design.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes PISA 2018 reading literacy using student-level contextual factors grounded in self-regulated learning (SRL). It imputes missing values in contextual factors using the median and excludes students with reading literacy scores below 262 (where PISA did not specify levels). For the outcome, it selects PV1READ as a single plausible value from the ten PISA plausible values. It first applies Shapley value decomposition to quantify relative contributions of factor categories and then trains a Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT) model, tuning learning rate (0.1) and using 10-fold cross-validation with an 80/20 train-test split. For the three top-performing economies (B-S-J-Z/China, Singapore, Macau), the GBDT reaches R2 = 0.49 (RMSE = 68.34), with Assessing credibility highest in importance; for all 79 countries/economies, R2 = 0.48 (RMSE = 73.26). The paper does not report complex-survey weighting or replicate-weight uncertainty, and the use of PV1READ limits how fully plausible-value uncertainty is represented.
